evals.prompt: We're a Series B B2B SaaS doing about $12M ARR selling a data observability product to engineering teams. Set me up to use the customer success skills.
evals.expected_output: One batched tappable question set, then a complete .agents/cs-context.md with all 15 sections, UNKNOWN markers on anything not supplied, a Source Inventory listing every family including absent ones, and a Coverage Ledger with a stated confidence cap.
assertions: Asks its questions as a single batched AskUserQuestion of no more than four, each with 2-4 options and the recommended one first and labelled
Creates or proposes .agents/cs-context.md
Contains all 15 numbered sections, including §15 Assumptions
Asks for segment boundaries as dollar values and captures the notice period and auto-renew default
Marks unsupplied fields as 'UNKNOWN — requires ...' rather than guessing
Does not substitute an industry benchmark for an unknown ARR/NRR figure
Ends with a Coverage Ledger and a maximum-confidence statement

evals.prompt: What data do I actually need connected before the churn prediction skill will give me something trustworthy?
evals.expected_output: The Source Inventory and Coverage Ledger sections only, with an explicit statement of which signal families gate which confidence level.
assertions: Runs in Data audit mode, not full Create mode
Enumerates all 12 source families
Explains the coverage-to-confidence cap relationship
Names which families most often cause a false-green read
Refers to the CS platform slot generically ('whichever platform holds your playbooks') and names no competing CS platform product
States that a partial connection set still produces a usable file with a capped confidence, rather than blocking

evals.prompt: Here's our context file from 8 months ago. We've since moved upmarket and killed the SMB plan.
evals.expected_output: A Refresh-mode diff that preserves hand-edited content, updates segments and coverage, bumps last_reviewed, and flags what else the segment change invalidates.
assertions: Detects the existing file and enters Refresh mode
Diffs rather than rebuilding from scratch
Asks only about what changed and re-asks nothing the existing file already answers
Bumps last_reviewed and next_review
Flags downstream sections invalidated by the segment change (coverage ratios, retention baseline, health model)
Records any default it proceeded on in the §15 Assumptions table with a named consequence

evals.prompt: Here's the account export RevOps sent me — it's a mess, there are title rows at the top and the ARR column has dollar signs in it. Can you use it to set up our CS context?
evals.expected_output: ingest.py run first, low-confidence mappings confirmed, an as-of date requested, and a partial context file with a coverage figure and a confidence cap — not a refusal.
assertions: Runs scripts/ingest.py on the file before quoting any number from it
Finds the real header row beneath the export preamble instead of failing to parse
Confirms every column mapping below 0.80 confidence before using those numbers
Asks for the export's as-of date and records it against the source in §9
Produces a partial file with a coverage percentage and a confidence cap rather than refusing on incomplete data
Records each default it ran on in the §15 Assumptions table with a concrete 'if wrong' consequence
